question: Which correctly describes a 'foundry' in the semiconductor industry?
choices: A company specializing in contract manufacturing of semiconductors designed by other companies
A company with no factories that specializes in semiconductor design and sales
A company specializing in selling parts for semiconductor manufacturing equipment
explanation: A foundry is a contract manufacturer (company or business) that fabricates wafers from circuit data designed by customer companies. Because advanced fabs requiring huge capital investment can be shared by many customers, the division of labor with fabless companies spread.

question: Which correctly describes a 'fabless' company?
choices: A company that handles everything from design to manufacturing and sales in-house
A company that has no manufacturing plants of its own and specializes in design and sales
A company that takes on only back-end semiconductor processes on contract
explanation: Fabless means a company without a manufacturing plant (fab). It concentrates its resources on design and sales and outsources manufacturing to foundries. A company that does everything from design to manufacturing in-house is called an IDM (integrated device manufacturer), and a company that does back-end work on contract is called an OSAT.

question: Which best describes 'Moore's law'?
choices: Clock frequency increases tenfold every 18 months
The number of transistors on an integrated circuit doubles every fixed period (about two years)
explanation: Moore's law is an empirical rule that the number of transistors on an integrated circuit doubles every fixed period. It was proposed in 1965 and later became widely known in the form of doubling about every two years. It is not a physical law but has served as a goal and benchmark for the industry's technology development.

question: Which correctly describes companies called OSATs?
choices: Companies that take on back-end processes such as semiconductor assembly and test on contract
explanation: OSATs (Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test) are companies that take on back-end processes such as semiconductor assembly (packaging) and test on contract. Together with foundries, which handle front-end processes on contract, and fabless companies, which specialize in design, they make up the industry's division of labor.

question: In the semiconductor market, what is the phenomenon called in which booms and busts repeat periodically due to the balance of supply and demand?
explanation: The silicon cycle refers to periodic booms and busts in which capital investment to meet rising demand leads to oversupply a few years later, followed by falling prices and curtailed investment, and then shortages again. Its period has been said to be roughly four years.

question: Which type of semiconductor company handles everything from design through front-end and back-end manufacturing to sales in-house?
explanation: An IDM (Integrated Device Manufacturer) handles design, manufacturing and sales in-house. It has the advantage of easy coordination between design and manufacturing but requires huge investment in fabs. IDMs are common in fields such as memory, power semiconductors and analog semiconductors.

question: Which correctly describes Dennard scaling?
choices: The number of transistors doubles about every two years
Shrinking transistor dimensions and supply voltage by the same ratio allows higher speed and integration while keeping power density constant
The semiconductor market repeats booms and busts on a cycle of about four years
explanation: Dennard scaling is the rule that shrinking transistor dimensions and voltage by the same ratio makes transistors faster and smaller while keeping power per unit area constant. In the mid-2000s, leakage current made voltage hard to lower, and scaling no longer followed this rule.

question: Which appropriately describes generation names (node names) of advanced processes such as the '3 nm generation'?
choices: They mean the gate length is exactly 3 nm
They mean the wafer thickness is 3 nm
In recent years, they have become generation labels that do not necessarily match physical dimensions such as actual gate length
explanation: Process generation names once roughly corresponded to dimensions such as gate length, but after the introduction of FinFETs and other changes, recent generation names have become labels indicating gains in performance and density, not directly tied to actual dimensions. The same name can mean different densities at different companies.

question: What is the scheme called in which a foundry puts designs from several customers on one wafer (one mask set) for prototyping?
explanation: An MPW combines several designs on one mask set and wafer, with participants sharing the mask and fabrication costs. Because masks for advanced processes are very expensive, MPWs are used by universities, startups and others to make prototypes at low cost.

question: Which appropriately describes investment in advanced semiconductor fabs?
choices: A cutting-edge fab can be built with a small investment (a few hundred million yen)
Manufacturing equipment such as exposure tools is expensive, and building an advanced fab can require investment on the scale of trillions of yen
Production relies mainly on manual labor with almost no manufacturing equipment
explanation: Manufacturing equipment is very expensive; a single advanced exposure tool can cost tens of billions of yen or more. Building an advanced fab can therefore require investment on the scale of trillions of yen, which has led to manufacturing being concentrated at foundries and to subsidy policies by governments.

question: What is an LSI called that integrates functions a system needs, such as a CPU, GPU, memory controller and communications, on a single chip?
explanation: An SoC is an LSI integrating many of the functions a system needs on one chip; smartphone processors are a typical example. It reduces part count and allows small size and low power. It is distinguished from an SiP, which houses multiple chips in one package.

question: What is an LSI called that is custom-designed for a specific application or customer?
explanation: An ASIC (Application Specific Integrated Circuit) is an LSI custom-designed for a particular product or application. Optimizing for only the needed functions gives advantages in performance and power, but development costs are high, so ASICs are used for products expected to sell in reasonable volumes.

question: Which category of semiconductor products, such as diodes, single transistors and power MOSFETs, performs a single function on its own?
explanation: Discrete semiconductors are products that function as a single device, such as diodes, transistors, thyristors, power MOSFETs and IGBTs. They are distinguished from integrated circuits (ICs), which integrate many devices on one chip. Many power semiconductors are supplied as discretes or modules.

question: Which correctly distinguishes the 'front end' and 'back end' of semiconductor manufacturing?
choices: The front end is design, and the back end is manufacturing
The front end builds circuits on the wafer, and the back end cuts out chips and assembles and tests them
The front end is testing, and the back end is wafer manufacturing
explanation: The front end builds circuits on wafers by repeating steps such as deposition, lithography, etching and ion implantation. The back end assembles chips cut from the wafer into packages, tests them and ships them. With advanced packaging growing in importance, the boundary between the two is becoming blurred.

question: What is the direction called that raises value not only by increasing integration through scaling but also by combining diverse functions such as sensors, power, analog and advanced packaging?
explanation: More than Moore, in contrast to 'More Moore', which pursues scaling, refers to raising functionality and added value through technologies other than scaling, such as sensors, MEMS, power, RF and advanced packaging. It is growing in importance as applications diversify, including IoT and automotive.

question: Which is an appropriate example of a field that has strongly boosted semiconductor demand in recent years?
explanation: With the spread of generative AI and the like, demand for GPUs and dedicated AI chips used in data centers, and the HBM paired with them, has grown rapidly. Electrification and growing functionality of cars, industrial equipment and IoT are other fields boosting semiconductor demand.

question: Which appropriately describes cutting-edge EUV exposure tools?
choices: Many companies supply them cheaply, and they are easy to obtain
Very few companies can supply them, and they are central to manufacturing advanced semiconductors
They are not used to manufacture advanced semiconductors
explanation: EUV exposure tools bring together advanced technologies such as light sources, multilayer mirrors and vacuum technology, and very few companies can supply production tools. They are very expensive and have become indispensable for manufacturing advanced logic and memory.

question: Which is an appropriate main reason governments are providing large-scale support to the semiconductor industry?
choices: Because demand for semiconductors has disappeared
Because semiconductors have become strategic goods essential to the economy and national security, and domestic supply chains need strengthening
explanation: Semiconductors are indispensable to every industry and to defense, yet manufacturing is concentrated in particular regions, so the risk of supply disruption has come to be recognized. Starting with the US CHIPS Act, Japan, Europe and others are providing large-scale support for attracting fabs and for research and development.

question: Which appropriately describes the role scaling has played in semiconductor cost?
choices: It has fit more transistors in the same area, lowering the cost per transistor
It has lowered manufacturing cost per wafer
It has reduced the number of transistors per chip
explanation: Scaling has raised manufacturing cost per wafer, but because far more transistors can be packed in, the cost per transistor has fallen. In recent years, cost increases for advanced processes have been large, and this trend is said to be slowing.

question: Which industry body develops standards for DRAM such as DDR?
explanation: JEDEC is an industry body that develops standards for semiconductor memory and other devices, defining DRAM standards such as DDR, LPDDR, GDDR and HBM. Common standards allow memory and processors from different makers to be used together. SEMI is an industry body dealing with standards for manufacturing equipment and materials.

question: Which region is known for an especially heavy concentration of contract (foundry) manufacturing of advanced logic semiconductors?
explanation: Contract manufacturing of advanced logic semiconductors is heavily concentrated in Taiwanese companies. This concentration is seen as a supply risk from disasters such as earthquakes and from geopolitical tension, and it is behind efforts to attract fabs to the US, Japan, Europe and elsewhere.

question: Which is commonly said to characterize the memory market?
choices: Prices tend to fluctuate greatly with the balance of supply and demand
explanation: DRAM and NAND flash are standardized products that are hard to differentiate between makers, so prices fluctuate greatly with the balance of supply and demand. Capacity investment during booms tends to cause oversupply during downturns, and memory makers' earnings tend to swing widely.

question: Which is an appropriate example of products designed by fabless companies?
explanation: Fabless companies design smartphone SoCs, GPUs, communications chips and the like, outsourcing manufacturing to foundries and assembly and test to OSATs and others. Silicon wafers are made by materials makers and exposure tools by equipment makers.

question: Which is an appropriate field in which Japan's semiconductor-related industry is said to have global strength?
choices: Manufacturing equipment and materials (wafers, resists, high-purity chemicals and gases, etc.)
explanation: Japan is said to have many companies with high global market shares in materials such as silicon wafers, photoresists and high-purity chemicals and gases, and in manufacturing equipment for cleaning, deposition, inspection and more. They occupy important positions in the semiconductor supply chain.

question: Which is an appropriate example of an issue facing the semiconductor industry in recent years?
choices: Shortages of engineers and technicians accompanying the construction of new fabs
Technology development is no longer necessary
explanation: With new fabs being built one after another around the world, securing people such as process engineers, equipment engineers and skilled production workers has become a major issue. Countries, companies and universities are working together to develop talent.

question: Which is closest to the approximate size of the global semiconductor market (annual revenue) in recent years?
choices: Several hundred billion dollars (tens of trillions to around 100 trillion yen)
explanation: The global semiconductor market has reached several hundred billion dollars per year in recent years. With growing demand for AI semiconductors for data centers and the like, further growth is expected. The market has expanded over the long term while repeating cycles of boom and bust.

question: Which is an appropriate reason the division of labor between foundries and fabless companies spread?
choices: Because investment in advanced fabs became huge, making it more efficient to separate design and manufacturing
explanation: Building an advanced fab requires huge investment, and it became hard to fill a fab with one company's products alone. Concentrating manufacturing at specialized foundries lets many customers share equipment, and design companies can focus on product development without owning fabs. This is how the division of labor spread.

question: Which is an appropriate reason the back end (packaging) has become more important in recent years?
choices: Because the back end is no longer needed
Because package cost has fallen to almost zero
Because chiplets and advanced packaging have become important means of raising system performance
explanation: As improving performance through scaling alone has become difficult, advanced packaging that connects multiple chips at high density has become a way to raise performance and power efficiency. For AI semiconductors, capacity for advanced packaging that combines HBM and processors has come to determine supply.

question: Which is an appropriate reason the amount of semiconductors in each car is increasing?
choices: Because electrification, driver assistance and information and communications functions have increased, using many more microcontrollers, power semiconductors, sensors and so on
Because electronics have disappeared from cars
explanation: Electric vehicles use power semiconductors in inverters that drive the motors, and driver-assistance systems need camera and radar sensors and high-performance processors. Infotainment and connectivity functions are also increasing, so the semiconductor content per car has grown greatly.

question: What is a company called whose business model is licensing design assets (IP) such as CPUs to other companies for fees?
explanation: IP vendors develop design assets such as CPU cores and interface circuits and license them to semiconductor companies, earning license fees and per-product royalties. Using IP lets semiconductor companies reduce development time and cost.
